extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (prosecution practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for handling restriction requirements, elections, traverses, withdrawn claims, and rejoinder during U.S. patent prosecution under 37 CFR and MPEP rules. Covers what applicants must do in replies and how examiners should treat claims and use form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse must be complete (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: A traverse to a restriction requirement must be a complete reply as required by 37 CFR 1.111: the reply must be reduced to writing, distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the examiner's action, and reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action; it must appear a bona fide attempt to advance the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere broad allegation that the requirement is in error does not comply. The applicant is required to specifically point out the reasons supporting the conclusion that the restriction requirement is in error. If the reply does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors, the election will be treated as an election without traverse (see MPEP § 818.03(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must make a provisional election (37 CFR 1.143)
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting reconsideration of a restriction requirement, the applicant must indicate a provisional election of one invention for prosecution; that invention shall be the one elected if the requirement becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election in reply to a requirement may be made with or without an accompanying traverse. The provisional election must identify the claims encompassing the elected invention (see form paragraph guidance in MPEP ¶ 8.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Election is made by applicant (not examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must make his or her own election; the examiner will not make the election for the applicant (37 CFR 1.142, 1.143).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This underscores that the applicant must explicitly elect; examiner only acts to acknowledge and to handle nonelected claims per regulations and MPEP procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: To preserve right to petition, applicant must traverse (37 CFR 1.144)
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve the right to petition a final restriction requirement to the Director, the applicant must have traversed the restriction (i.e., distinctly and specifically pointed out errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition from a requirement for restriction may be deferred until after final action on or allowance of elected claims but must be filed not later than appeal. A petition will not be considered if reconsideration (37 CFR 1.143) was not requested (see § 1.181). If applicant failed to distinctly and specifically point out errors, election treated as without traverse and right to petition is generally lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete or nonspecific traverse → election treated as without traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reply does not distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the restriction requirement, the election shall be treated as an election without traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should notify applicant using form paragraph 8.25.02 (Election Without Traverse Based on Incomplete Reply). An election without traverse generally means the applicant has not preserved the right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse asserting lack of patentable distinctness should supply evidence or admission
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant traverses on the ground the inventions or species are not patentably distinct, applicant should submit evidence or identify evidence of record showing the inventions/species are obvious variants or clearly admit that fact on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner finds one invention unpatentable over the prior art, that evidence or admission may be used in a 35 U.S.C. 103(a) rejection of the other invention. Failure to present evidence/admission can harm applicant's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traverse limited to nonallowance of linking claims = conditional agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Election of a single invention combined with a traverse only to the nonallowance of linking claims is an agreement with the Office's position that restriction is proper if the linking claim is not allowable and improper if it is allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office allows the linking claim, it must withdraw the requirement and act on all linked inventions that depend on the allowable linking claim. If all linking claims are canceled, 37 CFR 1.144 may not apply because record shows agreement with restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office generally does not permit shifting inventions after election and action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office policy is not to permit the applicant to shift to claiming another invention after an election is made and action given on the elected subject matter; an RCE cannot be used as a matter of right to switch inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions/nuances: a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) that is a continuation (not a divisional) carries over an express election made in the parent application unless applicant indicates otherwise. See Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Pharmachemie BV for case law nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims held to be drawn to nonelected inventions (withdrawn under 37 CFR 1.142(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims held to be drawn to nonelected inventions are withdrawn from further consideration pursuant to 37 CFR 1.142(b); examiner should clearly set forth reasons why the withdrawn claims are not readable on the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may traverse under 37 CFR 1.143. If a final restriction is made, applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.144. Examiners should treat withdrawn claims as directed in MPEP §§ 821.01–821.04 and use the appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 8.05 for claims withdrawn with traverse; 8.06 for without traverse).

rubrics_metrics.name: When initial requirement traversed, examiner must reconsider and reply to arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the initial restriction requirement is traversed, the examiner should reconsider the requirement; if still of the opinion restriction is proper, it should be repeated and made final in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making restriction final after traversal, examiner should reply to applicant's reasons/arguments and use form paragraph 8.25 (Answer to Arguments With Traverse) explaining why traversal was not persuasive and making the requirement final.

rubrics_metrics.name: If examiner withdraws restriction (in whole/part), must state rejoin groups and act on merits
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner determines restriction is improper in whole or in part, the next Office action should clearly state the restriction is withdrawn, specify which groups have been rejoined, and give an action on the merits of all claims directed to the elected invention and any rejoined invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.45 (and 8.46/8.47 variants as appropriate) to notify applicant when rejoining claims. Rejoined claims must be examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reply to a final action must include cancellation of nonelected claims or other appropriate action (37 CFR 1.144)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a final restriction exists and nonelected claims remain withdrawn with traverse, a complete reply to the final rejection must include cancellation of the nonelected claims or other appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.24 (Reply to Final Must Include Cancellation of Claims Non-elected with Traverse). If application otherwise ready for allowance, applicant is given ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer) to cancel noted claims or take other appropriate action; failure to act will be treated as authorization to cancel by examiner's amendment and pass the case to issue. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not permitted in that scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election without traverse consequences (loss of petition right and treatment of nonelected claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the election is made without traverse (including due to incomplete traverse), applicant generally does not retain the right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144; nonelected claims are withdrawn and may be canceled by examiner's amendment if application otherwise ready for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 8.25.01 or 8.25.02 to acknowledge election without traverse; use form paragraph 8.06 (Claims Stand Withdrawn Without Traverse) and 8.07 (Ready for Allowance, Non-elected Claims Withdrawn Without Traverse) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims added after an Office action directed to a different invention (37 CFR 1.145)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims added by amendment after an Office action that are directed to an invention independent of the originally claimed invention should be treated per 37 CFR 1.145: the applicant will be required to restrict to the invention previously claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exam action should include form paragraph 8.04 (Election by Original Presentation). An amendment canceling all claims to the elected invention and presenting only claims to a nonelected invention is nonresponsive — use form paragraph 8.26 and give applicant one month (30 days) to correct; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available for the correction period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder eligibility: must depend from or require all limitations of an allowable claim
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for rejoinder, a claim to a nonelected invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim (generic, linking, or subcombination claim). A withdrawn claim that does not require all the limitations of an allowable claim will not be rejoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should amend nonelected claims during prosecution to require the limitations of the elected invention to retain the right to rejoinder. Rejoinder between product and process claims requires that process claims depend from the allowable product claim limitations as appropriate (see MPEP § 821.04(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoined claims must be fully examined and meet patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejoined claims must be fully examined for patentability in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104 and must meet the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejoined claims are found unpatentable (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph), MPEP § 706.07 governs whether an Office action may be made final; timing of rejoinder (relative to first Office action on the merits) affects finality decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of restriction removes 35 U.S.C. 121 protections; watch for double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the restriction requirement is withdrawn, the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 121 are no longer applicable; claims presented in continuation/divisional applications that are anticipated by or include all limitations of an allowable claim may be subject to provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should call applicant's attention to potential double patenting and the possible need for a terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321(c)). See In re Ziegler and MPEP § 804.01 for guidance and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and procedural rule cross-references for amendments and IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments submitted after final rejection are governed by 37 CFR 1.116; amendments after allowance by 37 CFR 1.312. IDS timing and fees (which can affect finality) are governed by 37 CFR 1.97(c) and 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rejoinder leads to new grounds (necessitated by applicant amendment or IDS filed within the time/fee rules), MPEP § 706.07 gives authority to make an Office action final in certain situations. Examiners should consult the cited CFR sections and MPEP provisions when handling amendments and timing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific form paragraphs to communicate status and actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should use the prescribed form paragraphs for various situations: e.g., 8.22 (Requirement for Election and Means for Traversal), 8.25/8.25.01/8.25.02 (election/traverse acknowledgments), 8.05/8.06 (claims withdrawn with/without traverse), 8.03/8.24 (in condition for allowance notices and replies to final), 8.04/8.26 (election by original presentation and nonresponsive amendment), 8.45–8.50 series (rejoinder/withdrawal notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting the correct form paragraph communicates the legal/consequential status (e.g., preservation of petition rights, cancellation risk, rejoin outcome) and provides the applicant with proper instructions and time periods. Examiner notes in form paragraphs indicate bracketed fields to populate and contextual rules to observe.
